heading: INT. SUDS AND SPIN LAUNDROMAT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SUDS AND SPIN LAUNDROMAT - NIGHT
Midnight.
The street outside is empty and dark.
Inside, one fluorescent light buzzes above a row of dryers, all of them still.
A single machine in the back tumbles slowly, the clothes inside going around and around.
Tom, 20s, sits on a plastic chair with a gym bag between his feet, a flashlight and a half-eaten granola bar in his lap.
He has not spoken in a long time.
On the other side of the room, a figure in a wet raincoat sits with her back to the wall, a hood pulled low.
THE STRANGER has been there since the power went out two days ago.
Neither of them has said why they are here.
Is that machine still working?
units.name: TOM

units.text: Just the one. I think it's on a different circuit.
units.name: THE STRANGER

units.text: Huh.
units.name: TOM

units.text: A long pause.
The dryer thumps.
Water drips somewhere behind the wall.
How much food do you have left?
units.name: TOM

units.text: Not a lot. Some crackers. A can of beans I can't open.
units.name: THE STRANGER

units.text: I have a can opener. On my keys.
units.name: TOM

units.text: Of course you do.
units.name: THE STRANGER
paren: a short breath that is almost a laugh

units.text: Tom stands, crosses the room, and holds out the keyring.
She takes it without looking up.
The can opens with a tiny, rusty squeak.
Thanks. I'm Dana, by the way.
units.name: THE STRANGER

units.text: Tom.
units.name: TOM

units.text: I know. It's on your bag.
units.name: DANA

units.text: Right.
units.name: TOM

units.text: They sit in silence for a while, the only sounds the dryer and the dripping water.
Dana eats a spoonful of beans, offers the can.
Tom takes it, eats, hands it back.
You think anyone's coming?
units.name: DANA

units.text: I don't know. Eventually.
units.name: TOM

units.text: Eventually is a long time.
units.name: DANA

units.text: It's all we've got.
units.name: TOM

units.text: The dryer finally slows.
It clunks, groans, and stops.
The room is utterly still.
Dana looks at the dead machine, then at Tom.
Well. At least the towels are warm.
units.name: DANA

units.text: Tom laughs, a real one, small and cracked.
Dana laughs too.
Outside, far off, a single siren starts up and fades away again.
